about: UI teaching only (doc 25 §7). Each mechanic's card has a title, purpose, at most three steps, its how-to clip (how_clip, built by production/explainers/howto/build.py), a guided first use (nudge) and the goal targets that first need it (first_targets). 'clip' is the optional science explainer. Examples use hypothetical different numbers; never a canonical answer.

spare_power.title: How to use spare sunlight
spare_power.purpose: A full battery cannot take more; compare useful places for the spare power.
steps: Check how much room remains in the battery.
Follow the spare-power arrow to another store or useful load.
Compare each forecast before choosing.
spare_power.nudge: Follow the arrow after the battery is full.
spare_power.relationship: A full store cannot take more. Another store or a useful load can use spare daylight power before it is lost. Compare what each route saves or does while the battery stays full.
spare_power.example: Different example - hypothetical, not Aurora's power setting: a practice battery already holds its full 12 energy units. A panel offers 5 more; the battery has room for 0. A practice radio test can use 3 of those incoming units now, leaving 2 unused. The battery stays at 12. Compare useful work done before surplus is lost; read Aurora's own forecast before choosing.

mission_table.title: How to plan a shift
mission_table.purpose: Try a plan safely; heat choices appear for dark shifts.
steps: Choose the air and light rows shown for this shift.
Read the crew notes and press Try it to compare the forecast.
Lock in only when you are ready; confirm to use the plan.
mission_table.nudge: Store air while sunlight would overflow.
mission_table.relationship: Daylight can charge a battery. In darkness, each device draws from that store; compare what remains after the shift.
mission_table.example: Different example - hypothetical, not your night plan: a store holds 9 battery units. A lamp needs 2 and a fan needs 1 for one shift. The total cost is 3; 9 minus 3 leaves 6. Repeat the subtraction for each later shift, then compare the remaining store with its reserve. Use your own forecast and crew notes for this night.

probe.title: How to check a reading
probe.purpose: Use known references before trusting a new sample.
steps: Read each reference label.
Compare the instrument with both references.
Recheck before measuring an unknown sample.
probe.nudge: Amara: check the instrument before trusting it.
probe.relationship: Two known reference points show an offset and a span. Recheck both before using an unknown sample.
probe.example: Different example - hypothetical, not your probe settings: a practice meter reads 20 on an empty reference and 40 on a full reference. Halfway between them is 30. That is a method for comparing references, not a setting for Aurora's instrument. Read your own reference labels.

evidence.title: How to compare evidence
evidence.purpose: Connect the current goal with a clue you can check.
steps: Read the goal and why it matters.
Inspect the marked object and its source.
Compare the observation with the question before choosing.
evidence.nudge: Compare the current goal with the marked object's evidence.
evidence.relationship: An observation says what was measured. A claim explains it. Check whether the evidence supports the claim before making a decision.
evidence.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice lamp is lit for 3 of 9 checks. That observation alone does not prove why it went dark. Compare the power record with the same times before making a claim. Use the evidence from your current scene.

move.title: How to move around Aurora
move.purpose: Walk between stations, benches and crew members at your own pace.
steps: Press W, A, S, D or the Left Stick to walk through the room.
Follow the soft floor path or room signs to reach the marked station.
Take your time — walking never runs down a hidden clock.
move.nudge: Use W A S D to walk toward the Mission Table or the crew.
move.relationship: Every room in Aurora connects through pressurised hatches. Moving closer to a person or console brings up its interaction prompt.
move.example: Different example - hypothetical: in a practice bay, walking within two steps of the bench highlights its name and key prompt.

look.title: How to look around
look.purpose: Turn the camera to inspect room signs, crew members and wall displays.
steps: Move the mouse, or use the Right Stick.
Center the camera on a crew member or station to read its label.
Turn on Reduced Motion in Settings if you prefer instant transitions.
look.nudge: Move the mouse to look around the room.
look.relationship: Looking around helps you spot the gold objective marker, wall status boards and crew stations before you commit a plan.
look.example: Different example - hypothetical: panning across a practice dome reveals both the air tank gauge on the left wall and the chamber lamp on the right.

use.title: How to use equipment and talk
use.purpose: Interact with highlighted consoles, plants, doors and crew members.
steps: Walk up to a highlighted station or crew member until the prompt appears.
Press E (or the South controller button) to talk, inspect or operate.
Press Esc at any time to step back without losing progress.
use.nudge: Press E when a station or crew member prompt is highlighted.
use.relationship: Using a station opens its real controls or conversation so you can observe readings before making a decision.
use.example: Different example - hypothetical: pressing E at a practice workbench opens its reading card; closing it with Esc leaves every setting unchanged.

journal.title: How to use the Expedition Journal
journal.purpose: Review your current goal, evidence, plant growth, decisions, people and science.
steps: Press J (or open Journal from the top bar) at any time.
Use the left tabs — Now, Evidence, Garden, Decisions, People and Science.
Open 'What now?' (H) whenever you want a spoiler-free nudge or explainer.
journal.nudge: Press J to open the Expedition Journal and check 'Now'.
journal.relationship: Reading the Journal pauses the clock. It keeps only what you have already observed or completed, with zero future spoilers.
journal.example: Different example - hypothetical: opening the Now tab during a practice shift lists the current room, why the task matters, and three optional hint steps.

goal.title: How to read your goal
goal.purpose: The goal card says what to do and why; What now helps when you are stuck.
steps: Read the goal card at the top left: the goal and why it matters.
Press H for What now: the goal, where it is, and a hint.
Ask for one hint step at a time; hints never change rewards.
goal.nudge: Press H to open What now.
goal.relationship: The goal card always names the next job. What now adds where it is and a hint ladder that never changes your rewards.
goal.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice goal reads 'Check the spare lamp' and why: 'the night shift needs light'.

station_strip.title: How to read the station strip
station_strip.purpose: See power, air and water change when a job uses them.
steps: Watch the top right after a job: the strip appears when a value changes.
Read each bar's word as well as its colour.
Let it fade while you walk; it returns when something changes or runs low.
station_strip.nudge: Watch the top right after this job.
station_strip.relationship: The strip only shows when a station value changes or runs low, so the view stays clear while you walk.
station_strip.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice lamp test lowers a battery bar by one step, and the strip shows it for a few seconds.

messages.title: How to read Messages
messages.purpose: Crew and Earth send short messages between jobs.
steps: Press M to open Messages.
Pick a thread on the left, then a message.
Press Esc to close; reading pauses the clock.
messages.nudge: Press M to read your messages.
messages.relationship: Messages connect the scenes. Some point at your current goal; none of them change a setting for you.
messages.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice thread holds one unread note from a crew member about a seat plan.

lock_shift.title: How to lock in a shift
lock_shift.purpose: A plan only counts once you lock it in and confirm it.
steps: Try the plan and read its forecast.
Press Lock in when the forecast looks safe.
Confirm to use the plan, or go back to change it.
lock_shift.nudge: Try the plan first, then lock it in.
lock_shift.relationship: Try it never changes the station. Lock in asks once more; only Confirm uses the plan.
lock_shift.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice plan forecasts 6 battery units left; locking it in asks for a confirm before anything changes.

payload_carrying.title: How to carry and stack supplies
payload_carrying.purpose: Carry each case to its marked slot, one at a time.
steps: Walk to a supply case and press E to pick it up.
Carry it to an outlined slot and press E to set it down.
Assisted mode lets you choose the cases without a timer.
payload_carrying.nudge: Pick up a case with E, then set it in an outlined slot.
payload_carrying.relationship: Each case you place counts in the plan's forecast. Nothing is lost if you stop early; the forecast shows what you delivered.
payload_carrying.example: Different example - hypothetical: two of four practice cases placed means the forecast counts two.

care_photo.title: How to take a care-round photo
care_photo.purpose: Line up today's photo with the last one so growth is easy to compare.
steps: Look at the faint earlier photo behind today's view.
Nudge today's view until the two line up.
Take the photo; it is filed with today's date.
care_photo.nudge: Line up the photo with the faint earlier one, then take it.
care_photo.relationship: Photos taken from the same place on different days show real growth, not a change of angle.
care_photo.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice sprout looks taller only because the camera moved; lining up the frames shows the true change.

pollination_route.title: How to move pollen
pollination_route.purpose: Move pollen between two sealed chambers without mixing the brushes.
steps: Choose the donor, the brush and the carrier for this step.
Try it and read the preview before anything moves.
Lock in, then reverse with the clean brush.
pollination_route.nudge: Choose this step's donor and brush, then try it.
pollination_route.relationship: Each direction has its own brush, and only one pressure boundary opens at a time.
pollination_route.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice flower pair uses brush 1 one way and brush 2 back, never the same brush twice.

recorder_history.title: How to read a recorder's history
recorder_history.purpose: Give each file the one value its own label supports.
steps: Read the photographed plate, date and channel labels.
Put one token in each empty slot.
Check the local copy before playing it.
recorder_history.nudge: Match each file's label to one token.
recorder_history.relationship: A recorded file is trusted only when every label agrees with an independent source. The original stays untouched.
recorder_history.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice tape labelled 'Channel 2' takes the channel 2 token, not the one that sounds familiar.

reference_gauge.title: How to find a fault with a reference gauge
reference_gauge.purpose: Check a warning with an independent gauge before moving any valve.
steps: Read each line on the reference gauge twice, ten minutes apart.
Inspect the places that could leak, a few at a time.
Isolate only the line that fell, then check it holds.
reference_gauge.nudge: Equip the reference gauge and read the lines.
reference_gauge.relationship: A falling reading on one line, with the others steady, points at that line. The gauge is independent of the panel warning.
reference_gauge.example: Different example - hypothetical: practice lines read 100, 100, 100, then 100, 96, 100 ten minutes later; only the middle line is falling.

harvest_ledger.title: How to keep the harvest ledger
harvest_ledger.purpose: Count the seeds and split them between planting and the reserve.
steps: Separate old evidence from today's mature pods.
Count every well before you split the seeds.
Write the planting and reserve numbers so they add up.
harvest_ledger.nudge: Count the wells before you split the seeds.
harvest_ledger.relationship: A ledger keeps the lineage: every seed is either planted or sealed in reserve, and the two add up to the count.
harvest_ledger.example: Different example - hypothetical: 5 practice wells of 4 seeds make 20; planting 8 leaves 12 in reserve.

eva_suit_scanner.title: How to read the scanner and slopes
eva_suit_scanner.purpose: Pulse the scanner to read the ground before you walk or drive on it.
steps: Hold F to pulse the scanner across the ground.
Read the numbered slope bands: 1 flat to 4 no-go.
Keep your suit reserve above the return line.
eva_suit_scanner.nudge: Hold F to pulse the scanner.
eva_suit_scanner.relationship: Slope bands come from measured heights. Steeper ground costs more energy and can be unsafe to cross.
eva_suit_scanner.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice ridge shows band 2 on the path and band 4 on its edge; the path is the safe line.

survey_markers_network.title: How to place markers and fixed lines
survey_markers_network.purpose: Markers and fixed lines make a route safe for every later trip.
steps: Carry a marker to the next site and press E to place it.
Anchor a fixed line on the steep stretch.
Open the Coverage Map to check each link.
survey_markers_network.nudge: Place the next marker at the outlined site.
survey_markers_network.relationship: Things you build stay. A marker in line of sight of the last one extends the network back to the station.
survey_markers_network.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice marker behind a ridge shows no link; one on the crest links both ways.

rover_route_planner.title: How to plan a rover trip
rover_route_planner.purpose: Pick a road the rover can drive and keep the return in the battery.
steps: Open the Route Planner and compare the routes.
Keep every stretch inside the slope limit.
Confirm only a route that leaves the return reserve.
rover_route_planner.nudge: Open the Route Planner and compare the routes.
rover_route_planner.relationship: The trip home costs energy too. A route is safe only if the battery still holds the return reserve at the far end.
rover_route_planner.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice route uses 40 of 100 units each way, leaving 20 for the reserve.

impact_flash.title: How to classify an impact flash
impact_flash.purpose: Tell a real impact flash from a detector fault.
steps: Compare more than one frame of each flash.
A real flash changes and fades; a fault stays the same.
Keep only flashes that both checks support.
impact_flash.nudge: Compare the frames before you classify a flash.
impact_flash.relationship: A meteoroid flash is brief and changes from frame to frame. A stuck pixel or glint looks the same in every frame.
impact_flash.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice spot that is equally bright in five frames is a detector fault, not an impact.

energy_budget.title: How to budget energy for darkness
energy_budget.purpose: Plan every dark segment so the essentials never go off.
steps: Keep the essential loads on in every segment.
Add other loads only where the battery allows.
Check the reserve that remains when the light returns.
energy_budget.nudge: Keep the essentials on in every segment first.
energy_budget.relationship: In darkness nothing recharges the battery. Each segment subtracts its loads; the reserve must survive to the last one.
energy_budget.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice battery of 12 runs 2 units of essentials for 4 segments and keeps 4 in reserve.

storm_shelter.title: How to shelter from a solar storm
storm_shelter.purpose: Get everyone behind shielding and watch the dosimeter.
steps: Follow the shelter plan: people first, then supplies.
Read the dosimeter: the dose rate and the total.
Stay sheltered until the storm level falls.
storm_shelter.nudge: Open the hazard panel and read the dosimeter.
storm_shelter.relationship: Water and regolith between you and the Sun slow the particles. Less time outside and more shielding mean a lower dose.
storm_shelter.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice dosimeter shows the rate dropping when the crew moves behind the water wall.

repeaters_coverage.title: How to use repeaters and the coverage map
repeaters_coverage.purpose: A signal needs a clear line from each repeater to the next.
steps: Open the Coverage Map.
Find the link that is broken or blocked by terrain.
Restore or move a repeater until every link shows clear.
repeaters_coverage.nudge: Open the Coverage Map and find the broken link.
repeaters_coverage.relationship: Radio travels in straight lines. Terrain between two repeaters blocks the link; a repeater on high ground restores it.
repeaters_coverage.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice chain of three repeaters fails at the second because a hill blocks it.

controller_links.title: How to replace the controller and check both links
controller_links.purpose: Swap the controller safely, then prove each link on its own.
steps: Isolate, test for zero, replace, close and restore power.
Lock the local link first, then the Earth link.
Accept only an exact reply.
controller_links.nudge: Isolate the power before you touch the controller.
controller_links.relationship: A relay works only when every link passes its own test. One good link does not prove the other.
controller_links.example: Different example - hypothetical: a practice relay passes its local check but the Earth echo returns one wrong character, so it is not accepted.
